domain: The unclassifiable status of the 'volunteer plant' — a self-sown crop that appears uninvited in agricultural fields, and what it reveals about the logic of taxonomic systems built for intention
topic: The unclassifiable status of the 'volunteer plant' — a self-sown crop that appears uninvited in agricultural fields, and what it reveals about the logic of taxonomic systems built for intention

movement.gist: Introduce the volunteer plant: seed dropped by a prior harvest, germinating unbidden the following season in a field now planted with something else. It is neither the sown crop nor a weed in the ordinary sense, since it is genetically identical to a cultivated variety, yet its presence was never chosen — agronomists disagree about what to even call it.

Try the category 'crop': volunteers are the same species/variety as intentional plantings, sometimes indistinguishable in the field. But this mutilates the case — a crop is defined partly by cultivation decisions (spacing, timing, input schedule) that the volunteer never received; treating it as crop ignores that it competes with and contaminates the actual crop's yield and purity.

Try the category 'weed': volunteers are unwanted, must be controlled, sometimes herbicide-resistant carryover from prior genetically modified plantings, making them a genuine agronomic hazard. But this too mutilates the case — 'weed' presumes an organism alien to the field's intended lineage, whereas the volunteer is the field's own prior self returning; here the convergence begins to surface, that the trouble is not the plant's ambiguous nature but taxonomy's assumption that a single harvest, a single field, a single season can be treated as the unit of classification.

The taxonomy turn: agricultural classification was built around the intentional act of sowing as the line between crop and not-crop — a system devised when almost everything germinating in a field could be traced to a deliberate choice. The volunteer exposes that this system quietly smuggled in an assumption (discrete seasons, discrete intentions) that no longer holds once land is farmed continuously and residual seed banks accumulate underground for years. State plainly: the volunteer is not a hard case for the crop/weed distinction, it is evidence that the distinction was never describing biology at all, but describing the will of the last person who touched the field.

primary.axis: whether the volunteer plant is defined by its origin (unplanted) or its function (behaves as crop, weed, or wild)

secondary.axis: whether the difficulty lies in the plant itself or in the classifying apparatus that requires a single sorting axis

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension supplies the convergence point: both category trials fail for the same underlying reason, which is that the taxonomy demands one sorting axis where the phenomenon requires several simultaneously

family_realization.note: Passage executes 'Category Refugee' with precision. Volunteer tested against crop (para 2: 'bloodline and none of the appointment'), weed (para 3: 'field's own former self'), third category (para 4: 'would fail on schedule'). Each mutilates. Ends on what taxonomies do: they 'never described a plant at all, only the intention of the last person to touch the ground.' Difficulty arises from the right source: the categorization framework itself, not the plant.

ending_behavior.note: Final paragraph executes 'Scale Exit' with aperture-widening. Jumps from plant object to 'the interval — the years the soil holds an instruction.' Closes by reframing the unsorted thing from seed to timespan, suspending argument between scales (individual season vs. field memory). Stance is reframe-displace, not resolution.

voice_consistency.note: Sustained 'Ironic Formalist' voice. High formal register ('discrete field-season,' 'the premise that seasons come discretely') with controlled irony: 'arrives in full evening dress,' 'the tidy managerial logic... is tidy and it is wrong.' No AI-essay register; prose stays austere and precise throughout.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(C): half_truth trap—weed case called 'stronger' but para 3 exposes incompatibility, making endorsement a misread. Q2(C): premature_closure—para 4 predicts third-category 'would fail,' reading hope as conclusion. Q4(B): adjacent_answer—hazard detail in para 3 weed argument, not crop refutation. Q5(A): causal_inversion—field remembers owner's lapsed intent, not originating intent. Traps are substantive, not lexical.

explanation_quality.note: Each wrong option tied to specific passage mechanism. Q1(C) cites para 3's incompatibility claim; Q2(C) quotes para 4's prediction of failure; Q4(B) locates hazard in para 3 not para 2. No 'not mentioned' or 'too extreme' filler. Q6 explanations name the author's stance against each alternative with textual grounding.

answers.reasoning: Both classifications are shown plausible then flawed, redirecting critique to the sorting system itself.
Passage explicitly concludes distinction only tracked intention of last person, not the plant.
Text says third category 'would fail on schedule' since flaw is discrete field-season framing, not category shortage.
Detail strengthens weed case first, later undercut by lineage argument revealing incompatibility.
Final line shifts focus from seed to interval, widening classification question to timespan/memory.
Author rejects both crop and weed verdicts, treating volunteer as evidence framework misdescribes reality.
